jobs.title: Director of Data Architecture
jobs.description:
Supplier.io is the data foundation that enterprises build their supplier decisions on. Fragmented, duplicated, and unreliable supplier data quietly limits the ROI of source-to-pay platforms, analytics, risk, and AI initiatives, so we resolve, enrich, and continuously maintain the industry's most complete supplier identity, then put it to work for the teams that buy and the suppliers themselves. Relied on by companies across the Fortune 2000 for accurate data, our platform helps corporate procurement, finance, and compliance teams manage their vendor master, source diverse and sustainable suppliers, and mitigate risk, all from one verified identity instead of a dozen disconnected systems.

Our solutions turn that foundation into action: accurate data and continuous maintenance for teams managing a fragmented vendor master, sourcing intelligence built resolving even the hardest-to-identify suppliers, small, local, and diverse businesses, for teams tracking sustainability and compliance, and direct visibility for the suppliers themselves into where they stand with the enterprises that buy from them. Whether you're resolving vendor records, sourcing alternatives, or measuring program results, Supplier.io transforms complexity into clarity, so teams can lead with confidence and build supply chains that deliver for both business and community.

For more information, visit www.supplier.io.

The Opportunity

The Director, Data Architecture owns the strategy, standards, and team behind how data moves through Supplier.io, from source systems and web-scraping pipelines through ingestion, transformation, and governed delivery into the warehouses and marts the rest of the business relies on. You'll operate as a peer to our other engineering leaders, setting data architecture direction jointly with the CTO, while staying accountable for the reliability, quality, and governance of every data workflow we run.

You'll lead two distinct groups: a Data Engineering team building new pipelines, models, and architecture, and a Data Operations Engineering team running and maintaining the processes already in production. In the near term, before the team and its processes are fully built out, this role is hands-on: you'll be designing pipelines, data models, and orchestration directly, not just directing from a distance.

What You Will Do

Data Architecture & Platform Strategy

Own the multi-year data architecture strategy across our data warehouses and operational data stores, including evolving toward a medallion (bronze, silver, gold) lakehouse model.
Design and own our data lake and warehouse architecture, including the formation and population of data marts that serve analytics, product, and stakeholder reporting needs.
Set the orchestration strategy and standards for all data workflows, including source ingestion, web-scraping pipelines, ETL/ELT, and automated workflow management, and standardize the tooling used across the function.
Own the infrastructure and administration behind our data warehouses and pipelines, including capacity, reliability, and cost.
Own data governance end to end: the policies, standards, and practices for data quality, lineage, access, retention, and classification across every system of record.

Team & Execution Leadership

Build, lead, and grow two functions: Data Engineering, building new pipelines, models, and architecture, and Data Operations Engineering, running and maintaining existing production data processes.
Decide how the function is organized as it scales, including when and whether to add management layers beneath you to run day-to-day execution.
Stay hands-on early: design and review pipelines, data models, and orchestration directly until the team is built out to carry that execution independently, and stay close enough to the technology afterward to make credible architecture calls.

Cross-Functional Partnership

Partner with engineering leadership to keep data architecture decisions aligned with company-wide standards.
Work closely with data engineering teams on technical planning and delivery for our core data products.
Partner with product, analytics, and other business stakeholders across the company to understand data needs and translate them into warehouse and data mart designs.

Data Quality & Compliance

Define and enforce data quality gates, lineage tracking, and auditability standards across all data pipelines.
Own data access controls, classification, and retention policy across the data estate.
Ensure compliance-relevant and audit-sensitive data is handled according to governance standards as our data sources and customer base grow.

What You Will Need To Succeed

10+ years in data engineering, data architecture, or related roles, including 5+ years in a Director or Manager-level leadership role owning architecture strategy and a team, not just individual delivery.
Deep, hands-on experience designing and operating cloud data warehouse or lakehouse architectures (Snowflake and/or BigQuery), including medallion (bronze, silver, gold) patterns.
Experience integrating a range of source systems (MongoDB, PostgreSQL, MySQL) and building ingestion and ETL pipelines from varied and unstructured sources, including web-scraping pipelines and background job orchestration.
A track record of building and scaling a data engineering or data platform organization, including deciding when and how to split engineering and operations functions.
Strong data governance background: establishing policies and standards for data quality, lineage, access, and retention in a regulated or compliance-sensitive environment.
Experience setting technical direction jointly with peer engineering leaders and influencing architecture decisions across teams.
Excellent communication skills, comfortable setting strategy with peer leaders and reporting data platform health, cost, and risk directly to the CTO.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience consolidating or re-architecting data platforms following an acquisition or significant data source expansion.
Experience with orchestration tooling such as Airflow or dbt, and with scraping or crawling infrastructure at scale.
Background establishing data marts and self-service analytics layers for non-engineering stakeholders.
Familiarity with data observability tooling (Monte Carlo, Great Expectations, Soda, or similar).

Euroclear Nordics AB is now looking for Head of Core Systems to lead an experienced specialist team responsible for business-critical IT environments. About The Role

As part of a leading provider of financial market infrastructure and post-trade services, you will work in an international environment where local expertise meets global perspectives. As Head of Core Systems, you will have overall responsibility for a team working with a business-critical mainframe environment. You will lead an experienced and close-knit team and ensure stable and secure IT operations with high availability requirements. The team consists of internal employees, consultants and external suppliers.

You will report to the Head of Infrastructure & Operations and have overall responsibility for the Core Systems team’s delivery, development and roadmap. The area includes technologies and platforms such as DB2, IMS, MQ and z/OS.

An important part of the role is to lead the team through an ongoing transformation in which technologies, platforms and ways of working are evolving. The position combines people leadership and change management with close involvement in operational matters.

We are looking for someone who has

Several years of leadership experience with people management responsibility within IT, infrastructure or operations.
Experience leading teams through change or transformation, with the ability to create a sense of stability and maintain engagement throughout the journey.
A good understanding of business-critical IT environments and the requirements associated with stability, security, structure and availability.
A solid overall technical understanding and confidence in leading and collaborating with technical specialists.
A structured and communicative approach, with the ability to work effectively with both technical teams and other parts of the organization.

Experience from banking, financial services or another regulated industry.

Experience working in IT environments with high security and availability requirements.

Personal qualities

You are a confident and present leader who creates trust, clarity and engagement. You are attentive and genuinely interested in your employees, while also being comfortable setting directions and making decisions.

You work in a structured and methodical way and can establish order and set priorities in a complex environment with several parallel activities. You are communicative and relationship-oriented and enjoy collaborating with both technical specialists and other parts of the organization.

At Euroclear Nordics AB, you will be part of a culture that values collaboration, innovation and continuous improvement. As part of a global organization, you will have excellent opportunities to work with colleagues around the world and gain valuable insight into international financial markets.

As part of the Euroclear team, you will work in a dynamic and collaborative environment where your contribution matters and where you are encouraged to grow and reach your full potential.

We are committed to supporting your success through continuous learning and development opportunities, knowledge sharing and collaboration with talented colleagues across the Euroclear Group. jobs.title: Vice President of Programs
jobs.description:
We’re Recruiting For…

Vice President of Programs

About the Centre 

The Confederation Centre is Canada’s National Memorial to the founders of the country. It is the result of a dream shared by all Canadians - a place where Canada’s evolution and multicultural character is celebrated and explored right where Canadian confederation began; where the talents of Canadian people are nurtured and showcased through arts, learning, and conversation. Taking up a full city block in downtown Charlottetown, the Centre includes performance venues, art gallery spaces, arts education and learning studios, and spaces for convening and conversation. 

Opened by Queen Elizabeth II in 1964 to commemorate the centennial of the 1864 Charlottetown Conference, the Confederation Centre has welcomed millions of visitors from Canada and the world to experience Canada through many lenses. Producing world-class theatre performances, gallery exhibitions, arts education, community programs, and convening opportunities for discussion on Canadian confederation, the Centre is the largest national multidisciplinary cultural institution in Atlantic Canada. 

Home to the Charlottetown Festival, which sells close to 100,000 tickets over 14 weeks each summer, the Centre employs more than 200 people and drives more than $30 million in economic activity for Prince Edward Island. The Centre is now completing the most signiﬁcant transformation in its history: a $65 million rejuvenation of the former library and archives complex, creating new facilities for the Palmer Institute for Canadian Leadership, the Arts Academy, and the Arts Innovation Hub. The Centre is governed by a national board of directors from across Canada. It is where people learn about Canada and explore the issues most important to us; it is Where Canada Connects. 

Charlottetown, Prince Edward Island 

The capital city of PEI is the birthplace of Canadian confederation, and the Confederation Centre of the Arts is Canada’s national memorial to those who met here in 1864 and proposed a union that would result in a new country three years later. Charlottetown is a beautiful place to live and work. It has a thriving cultural community with numerous attractions including arts, recreation, restaurants, parks, and the harbour. Charlottetown is home to the University of Prince Edward Island and Holland College, and welcomes roughly 1.5 million tourists every summer. Minutes away are some of the best beaches, golf courses, and natural attractions that Canada has to oﬀer. 

The Opportunity

The Confederation Centre is seeking a Vice President of Programs, to lead and support all of the Centre’s public programming. Reporting to the Chief Executive Oﬃcer, the Vice President of Programs provides leadership to the program directors and staﬀ in Theatre, Art Gallery, Arts Academy, Palmer Institute for Canadian Leadership, Archives, and the Arts Innovation Hub, to ensure sustainable operations and positive impact locally, regionally, and nationally.  

As the Centre completes the most signiﬁcant expansion in its history, its programming is growing in scale and in range. The Vice President will ensure this growth is coordinated, ﬁnancially sustainable, and aligned with the Centre’s Strategic Plan, so that every program contributes to the Centre’s national mandate and mission.  

As a key member of the senior leadership team, the Vice President serves as a trusted advisor to the CEO on program strategy, and works closely with the VP of Finance, VP of Operations and Infrastructure, and the full leadership teams in development, marketing, communications, and HR. This is an exceptional opportunity for an experienced cultural leader to shape the next chapter of a beloved national institution. 

Areas of Oversight 

• Theatre
including the Charlottetown Festival, and year-round performing arts programming
• Art Gallery
including the six gallery spaces, permanent collection, and community programming
• Arts Academy
including a host of programs in dance, musical theatre, choir, and visual arts
• Palmer Institute for Canadian Leadership
including convening programs for dialogue on Canada
• Arts Innovation Hub
including artist residencies and production support for new work
• Archives
including the organization and use of historic documents and artifacts of the Centre

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership 

Provide strategic and operational support to the leadership team across theatre, visual art, arts education, leadership and convening, and archives that advances the Centre’s national mandate and Strategic Plan
Serve as a trusted advisor to the CEO on program direction, priorities, and risk, and support the CEO and CFO in reporting to the Board of Directors and its committees

Purpose

The Scotiabank Strategy group is a central team focused on shaping the Bank’s strategic agenda, considering both enterprise-wide and business / function-specific strategic questions and opportunities.

Reporting to the Vice President, Enterprise Strategy, the Director, Enterprise Strategy
is a key representative for GBM at the Enterprise Strategy level. The Director plays a critical role in supporting the contextualization of GBM strategy within the context of the Bank’s overall strategic framework. The Director also works closely with GBM leadership, Enterprise Strategy partners, and Corporate Functions to deliver strategic insights and, support strategic planning and execution as needed across GBM. The role focuses on shaping strategic direction, translating strategic direction into actionable initiatives, providing analytical rigor, and ensuring strategies are practical, measurable, and executable.

The incumbent combines strong strategy development capabilities and experience in a top-tier strategy consulting or corporate strategy environment with either experience in Corporate & Investment Banking, Capital Markets, and/or related businesses, or a demonstrated ability to rapidly build domain expertise in complex industries. The successful candidate will be expected to quickly develop a deep understanding of GBM businesses, products, clients, and market dynamics and engage credibly with senior business leaders on strategic priorities.

Is this role right for you? In this role, you will be involved in:

Strategy Development & Planning Support

Support the development and refresh of GBM strategy in alignment with the Bank’s enterprise strategy, helping to “connect the dots” across business lines and corporate functions.
Lead discrete strategic workstreams and targeted deep dives across GBM strategic priorities, including growth, profitability, client experience, and operating model initiatives.
Identify, assess, and evaluate strategic opportunities and issues specific to GBM, including implications of market trends, competitive dynamics, regulatory developments, and emerging risks.

Provide structured analytical support and strategic recommendations to senior leaders, under the guidance of the VP.

Design strategic KPIs and tracking mechanisms to monitor progress against GBM strategic objectives.
Conduct benchmarking and competitive analysis against local and global peers to identify performance gaps, opportunities, and emerging best practices.

Contribute to the preparation and facilitation of GBM and enterprise strategy offsites, planning sessions, and leadership workshops.
Stay current on global capital markets, investment banking trends, and broader financial services developments to inform strategic thinking.

Build strong working relationships with GBM leadership, enterprise strategy colleagues, and partners across finance, risk, technology, and other corporate functions.
Bridge silos and enable alignment across teams to support execution of GBM priorities.

About The Role

We're seeking a Director of Product Support Operations to lead the team that runs how Tubi's Tech Org plans, executes, and ships. PSO is a deliberately lean, AI-first team of Technical Program Managers and Customer Experience specialists built around three durable jobs: orchestrating agentic systems, people, and the cross-team programs that land Tubi's most complex initiatives for over 100 million monthly active users.

You will own the Tech Org's most complex, company-level programs, spanning live events, platform integrations, monetization, and financial operations, along with the agentic systems that carry the org's operational load. You will also own the customer experience function end to end and run the Tech Org's operating cadences, including planning cycles, executive business reviews, and org-wide communications. You'll work closely with engineering, product, design, data science, and finance leaders as a trusted executive partner.

This team consists of builders, not just coordinators. If you're passionate about building with AI rather than coordinating around it, landing complex programs at company scale, and developing world-class talent while staying hands-on yourself, this is the role for you.

This is a hybrid role based out of our San Francisco, New York, Los Angeles, or Toronto offices.

What You'll Do

Define the multi-year strategy and 12-month roadmap for Product Support Operations, aligning the portfolio with company objectives
Lead, develop, and recruit high-performing Technical Program Management and Customer Experience team members, setting a high bar through direct feedback and rigorous performance management
Operate as a player-coach: personally design, ship, and maintain agentic workflows and lead high-stakes programs while modeling the builder-TPM standard for the function
Own execution of the Tech Org's most complex, company-level programs spanning multiple organizations and external partners, with impact validated by metrics
Define the org's AI-enabled operating model to scale the organization without adding operational overhead
Own the customer support operating model end to end, positioning the voice of the customer as a reliable input to executive planning with clear evidence and confidence standards
Implement and lead the execution systems that raise delivery quality across the Tech Org, including planning cycles, weekly and monthly business reviews, and org-wide communications
Act as a trusted advisor to executives, driving alignment on company-level priorities and securing the resources to deliver them

Your Background

7+ years of technical program management or operations experience, including 4+ years leading and developing teams
Proven track record of landing complex, multi-org programs end to end with measurable company-level impact
A builder at heart: a hands-on record of designing, shipping, and maintaining agentic workflows or automations (agents, skills, prompt engineering), not just managing teams that use them
Deep technical fluency: able to engage engineering executives credibly on feasibility, architecture tradeoffs, and sequencing
Player-coach leadership style: you delegate and develop others while continuing to build and deliver yourself
Strong portfolio management judgment, including prioritization against company strategy and disciplined decisions on what to start, stop, and consolidate
Executive-level communication and influence, with a track record of driving alignment across organizations with competing priorities
Experience leading customer experience, support operations, or voice-of-customer programs is a plus
Experience in streaming, media, or consumer technology at scale is a plus
